sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 06.08.2017 at about 5.00 p.m. the deceased - S.B.Kiran Kumar was traveling in a Maruthi Van bearing registration No.KA-53-M-1713, the said vehicle met with an accident near Chowdadenahalli Gate on Malur - Kolar Road with one Mahindra Bolero Max vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-7906, because of which the deceased got injured and was admitted to hospital, but succumbed to injuries on 11.08.2017.
The Tribunal has concluded that the driver of Mahindra Bolero Max Vehicle was responsible NC: 2023:KHC:29011 to an extent of 85% for causing of the accident and the deceased was responsible for the balance 15%.
The Mahindra Bolero Max Vehicle was duly insured with respondent No.2- Insurance Company at the time of the accident.

The Tribunal, after deducting the amount towards contributory negligence has awarded a compensation of Rs.15,07,000/- along with interest at the rate of 7%
p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioners who are legal representatives of the deceased have preferred this appeal.
4. The accident occurred in the year 2017.
The petitioners have not established the income of the deceased before the Tribunal.

Hence, it is deemed appropriate to fix his income notionally as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority in consultation with Insurance Companies which will be Rs.11,000/- per month.
The deceased was aged 32 years at the time of the accident.

Hence, a multiplier of '16' is NC: 2023:KHC:29011 adopted as per the law laid down by the Apex Court in SARLA VERMA & ORS V. DELHI TRANSPORT CORP.& ANR reported in 2009(6)
SCC 121].

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Taking the income of the deceased at Rs.11,000/- per month, 40% has to be added to his income towards future prospects as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD.
V. PRANAY SETHI reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.
Further, the deceased, who had four dependants at the time of his death 1/4th of his income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.

Thus, on the count of 'loss of dependency', the petitioners would be entitled to a sum of Rs.22,17,600/- (11,000 x12x16+40%x3/4).
5.
Petitioners are also entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards 'loss of estate and funeral expenses'.

6. Petitioners are all entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards 'loss of consortium' and thus together are entitled to Rs.1,60,000/- (40000x4) under this head.
NC: 2023:KHC:29011 7.
The Tribunal based on actual bills has granted a sum of Rs.90,000/- towards medical expenses incurred for treating the deceased before he died.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
8. In the course of the arguments, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that he does not challenge the contributory negligence attributed to the deceased.

Thus, 15% has to be deducted from Smt. R. Mala vs Sri. E. Anil Kumar on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44839257/

sentences.text: the total compensation amount calculated above.
9. Thus, the petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.21,22,960/-(24,97,600x85%) as against Rs.15,07,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, the petitioners are together entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.6,15,960/- over and above what has been awarded by the Tribunal (Rs.21,22,960 minus Rs.15,07,000/-).
Further, given the bank rate of interest, I deem it appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced NC: 2023:KHC:29011 compensation from the date of petition till realization.
